Bake bread approximately 30 minutes or until dough is golden and firm to touch. Internal dough temperature should register approximately 190° - 205°.

sources.name: Flaky Biscuits

lines.name: chilled unsalted butter or 7 tablespoons chilled coconut oil
melted butter
lines.notes: optional, for non-vegan biscuits; for brushing on top

steps: Preheat oven to 375° F and line half-sheet tray with parchment paper.
Sift flours, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon (if using) in medium sized bowl. Whisk to combine.
Cut fat into flour mixture until fat is crumbly and coated in flour. Crumbles should be about size of small peas or smaller.
Pour in milk or almond milk and gently mix with rubber spatula just until combined, being careful to not over-mix.

Transfer dough to lightly floured table and gently roll out to shape of rectangle, about 1/4 inch thick. With long edge facing you, fold in both short ends to meet in middle. Fold dough forward in half and very gently roll together to 3/4 inch or no thinner than 1/2-inch square. This folding technique will provide flaky layers if not over-worked and too flat.
Cut biscuits with lightly floured cookie cutter or sharp knife and transfer to sheet tray. If desired, brush tops with melted butter.
Bake for about 6 minutes and rotate pan in oven to ensure even browning. Continue baking for about another 10 minutes or until golden brown on top and slightly firm to touch.
Transfer to rack and cool.
Note: Brushing with coconut oil in place of butter is not recommended.

sources.name: Zucchini Bread
steps: Heat convection oven to 350° F. Line a 4 1/2 x 9-inch loaf pan with parchment.
Whisk together flax mixture, canola oil, vanilla, and rice vinegar in bowl. Stir in zucchini and pecans. Set aside.
In separate bowl, sift together coconut sugar, cinnamon, salt, baking soda, baking powder, all-purpose flour and whole wheat pastry flour.
Whisk wet ingredients into dry. Pour batter into loaf pan and bake for 55 minutes.
Let bread cool completely before slicing and serving.

sources.name: Gluten-Free Feta-Dill Quick Bread
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix together flour, baking powder, and salt in large bowl.
In separate bowl, combine olive oil, milk, egg, and feta cheese. Add wet mixture to dry, and mix dough to combine. Add dill.
Pour batter into muffin molds and immediately transfer back to oven to bake.
Bake for at least 30-40 minutes. Bread is ready when toothpick inserted in bread comes out clean.

sources.name: GLUTEN-FREE BANANA BREAD
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
In large bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
In separate medium bowl, whisk together butter, maple crystals, egg, mashed bananas, vanilla extract, and buttermilk.
Whisk wet ingredients into dry. Fold together, making sure to scrape bottom of bowl to mix well. Pour dough into prepared muffin molds.
In small saucepan, melt butter for crumble. Combine butter, maple crystals, and rolled oats in bowl. Transfer crumble to top of bread.
Bake for 30-45 minutes, or until toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean. Remove from oven and allow to rest in pan for 15 minutes, before inverting onto wire rack to cool completely.

sources.name: Pizza Dough #2

lines.name: rice syrup or honey or maple syrup

steps: In medium bowl, mix sponge ingredients together with whisk.
Let sponge sit 20-30 minutes covered with plastic wrap in warm place.
Add salt, oil and water to sponge, then add flours in 1/2 cup increments until incorporated.
Knead about ten minutes. Let pizza dough sit 40 minutes covered with plastic wrap in warm place.
Preheat oven to 475°F.
Place pizza stone in oven to heat up at least 30-40 minutes before baking.
Transfer pizza to peel before adding sauce and topping.
Bake on stone 8-10 minutes, turning once at half-way point.

sources.name: Spelt Pizza Dough

lines.name: rice syrup or honey or maple syrup

steps: In medium bowl, mix sponge ingredients with whisk.
Cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 20 to 30 minutes in warm place.
Add water, salt, and oil to sponge, and mix together with wooden spoon. Add flour in 1/2 cup increments.
Remove dough from bowl, form dough into ball and knead on floured work surface. Dough should be soft and a little sticky. Knead for about 10 minutes.
Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic and place in warm spot until doubled in size, about 40 minutes. Punch down, shape dough and bake.
Preheat oven to 475°F. Place pizza stone in oven to heat up at least 30-40 minutes before baking.
Transfer pizza to peel before adding sauce and toppings.
Bake on baking stone 8-10 minutes, turning once at half-way point.

sources.name: Gluten-Free, Egg-Free Mini Pizzas
steps: Line 2 half-sheet trays with Silpats or parchment generously brushed with olive oil.
In medium bowl, dissolve maple crystals in water and add yeast. Set aside.
In another medium bowl, sift and whisk together rice flour, tapioca flour, and xanthan gum. Add fennel seeds and salt, and mix together. Set aside.

In small pot, add flax seed to boiling water and simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until water reaches consistency of egg white. Strain mixture through fine-meshed sieve, and retrieve 2 tablespoons of seedless extract. Set aside.
In stand mixer, blend flaxseed extract, 1 tablespoon olive oil and yeast-maple crystal water. Add flour mixture and beat on high for 2 minutes.
Using tablespoon, dollop batter onto baking sheets, making 6-8 mini pizzas per sheet tray. With circular motion, spread each circle out with spoon to about 2 inches in diameter.
Cover with inverted baking sheet, and let rise 40-45 minutes. Preheat oven to 375°F.
Bake each mini pizza 10 minutes without toppings.
Remove trays from oven, and garnish pizzas with toppings of choice. Dribble remaining oil over each mini pizza. Bake another 10 minutes to cook fillings and melt cheese, if using.

sources.name: Whole Wheat Pizza

lines.name: rice syrup or honey or maple syrup

steps: In medium bowl, mix sponge ingredients with whisk.
Cover with plastic wrap and rise for 20-30 minutes in warm place.
Add water, salt and oil to sponge. Mix together with wooden spoon. Add flour in 1/2 cup increments.
Remove dough from bowl, form into ball and knead on floured work surface. Dough should be soft and pliable. Knead for about 8-10 minutes.
Place dough in lightly-oiled bowl, cover with plastic and place in warm spot until doubled in size about 40 minutes. Punch down, shape dough and bake.
Preheat oven to 475°F. Place pizza stone in oven to heat up at least 30-40 minutes before baking.
Transfer pizza to peel before adding sauce and toppings.
Bake on pizza stone from 8-10 minutes, turning once at half-way point.

sources.name: FOCACCIA WITH HERBS

lines.name: small cooked
lines.notes: peeled and mashed potato, room temperature

steps: For sponge: Make sponge by mixing yeast, sweetener, water, and high-gluten flour together.
Cover sponge with plastic, transfer to warm place until doubled in size (20-30 minutes).
For dough: Preheat oven to 475°F. Place pizza stone in oven to heat up.
Incorporate into sponge mixture: potato, warm water, olive oil, salt, semolina flour, fresh herbs, and enough whole wheat bread flour to form knead-able dough.
Transfer dough to floured work surface and knead. Dough should be soft and a little sticky. Knead for about 10 minutes.
Transfer dough to oiled bowl, cover with plastic. Rise until doubled in size (30-45 minutes).
Fold and turn dough. Flatten and form focaccia on parchment-lined pizza peel. Cover with damp towel and let rise again 15-20 minutes more, or until doubled in size again.
Brush top of focaccia with olive oil and sprinkle with mixture of fresh herbs, sea salt, and fresh cracked pepper. Dimple surface with fingertips, and transfer to pizza stone. Bake 20-25 minutes.

sources.name: FOCACCIA

lines.name: unbleached white flour or 1/2 white and 1/2 whole wheat bread flour

steps: For the sponge: In medium bowl, mix sponge ingredients (yeast, rice syrup or honey, lukewarm water, and hi gluten flour) with whisk. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise for 20-30 minutes in warm place.
For the crust: Add potato, water, oil and salt to bowl with sponge. Add flour in 1/2 cup increments.
Remove dough from bowl, form dough into ball and knead on a floured work surface. Dough should be soft and a little sticky. Knead 8-10 minutes.

Place dough in lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic, and place in warm place until doubled in size - about 1 hour. Punch down, transfer to parchment-lined sheet pan and let rise 15 to 20 minutes more.
Preheat oven to 475° F.
Transfer focaccia to pan. Dimple surface of focaccia with fingers before adding toppings.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes.

sources.name: Apple Phyllo Roll

lines.name: coconut sugar
lines.notes: buzzed to powder in coffee grinder

lines.name: walnuts
lines.notes: oven-roasted and ground in food processor to breadcrumb texture

steps: Preheat conventional oven to 400°F (convection oven will dry phyllo too much).
Prepare large bowl of water and add lemon juice. Peel, core, and thinly slice apples to 1/8-inch thickness and transfer them to lemon water to prevent browning.

Drain apples in colander. In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add apples, coconut sugar, and cinnamon. Sauté apples on medium heat until they release most of their moisture and become tender, stirring frequently. Transfer apples to bowl to cool.

Unroll phyllo on work surface and cover with damp cloth. To assemble, lay one sheet of phyllo on parchment paper horizontally. Brush sheet with oil and sprinkle lightly with small amount of walnuts. Repeat process, stacking and brushing another 3 sheets.

Spoon apple mixture horizontally along bottom of phyllo, leaving 1-inch border on bottom and 2 inches on left and right side. Fold in left and right sides over filling, then roll phyllo from bottom to top to form log. Repeat steps 5-7 for the second phyllo roll.
Score both rolls halfway through on bias into 8 equal portions. Brush roll with remaining oil.
Transfer rolls to parchment-lined sheet tray and bake for 30-35 minutes or until golden.
Cool ten minutes, then slice all the way through pre-scored cuts. Serve with Lemon and Maple-Flavored Yogurt (recipe below).

sources.name: APPLE RING

lines.name: apples
lines.notes: peeled, cored, and cut into medium dice

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. In large bowl, combine yeast, water, apple juice, rice syrup, and 2 cups all-purpose flour; stir until smooth. Cover sponge and set aside in warm place for 30-45 minutes.
Add melted oil, salt, and maple crystals. Mix together all-purpose and whole wheat pastry flours. Add flour, cup-by-cup until dough is formed that pulls away from sides of bowl.
Knead dough on table about 10-15 minutes, using remaining flour until smooth dough forms.

Transfer dough to large, clean, lightly oiled bowl and cover with plastic wrap. Proof in warm place for 45-60 minutes or until dough has doubled in size. While dough is proofing, prepare two half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Turn/fold dough. Rise one more time.

Divide into two equal portions. Roll out first dough into rectangle about 1/4” thick. Pull edges of dough to create a rectangular shape. Spread half of apple filling across near end of dough horizontally. Fold dough over filling and roll log forward until seam is on bottom. Attach ends of dough to create ring. Move ring to prepared baking sheet. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.

Loosely cover rings with damp towel and set aside in warm place. Rise until dough has doubled in size, about 15-20 minutes. Cut 5-6 slits (steam vents) in top of each ring. Glaze each ring with maple syrup.
Transfer bread to oven and bake approximately 30-45 minutes or until dough is thoroughly browned. Cool rings completely before serving.

sources.name: Sticky Buns
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Whisk together syrup ingredients, combine raisin-walnut filling; set both aside.
In large bowl, combine warm water, maple syrup, and yeast. Proof for 5-10 minutes, or until yeast is activated (foamy). Add melted coconut oil.
In separate large bowl, whisk together flours and salt.
Add enough flour mixture to yeast mixture to create dough that pulls away from sides.
Knead dough about 10 minutes to form soft, smooth dough, using flour as necessary.
Transfer dough to clean, large bowl. Cover with plastic wrap, and rise until doubled in size (about 30 minutes to 1 hour).
Fold/turn dough. Rise one more time.

Cut dough in half and roll each half to 1/4-inch thick rectangle. Spread 1/3 syrup mixture over dough. Sprinkle 1/2 raisins and walnuts on top. Roll dough into cylinder. Repeat process with second dough.
Cut rolled dough into 2-inch rounds and arrange nestled in two oiled 9-inch cake pans lined with parchment.
Rise dough until doubled in size, approximately 15-20 minutes.
Bake for 25 minutes. Brush remaining 1/3 syrup mixture on top, rotate pans, and bake for 10-15 minutes more or until firm to touch and golden. Cool and unmold.

sources.name: CRANBERRY WALNUT SCONES

lines.name: almond milk soured with 1 tablespoon lemon juice

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line half-sheet pan with parchment.
In medium bowl, stir together flours, maple crystals, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
With pastry cutter, cut butter into dry ingredients until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add cranberries, nuts, and zest.
Make well in center and gradually stir in milk, ginger juice, and maple syrup just to combine. Do not over mix; dough should be sticky and difficult to work with.
On lightly floured surface, pat or roll dough to 1/2 inch thickness. Cut into shapes and place on sheet pan. Brush tops with milk and sprinkle with maple crystals.
Bake 12-15 minutes or until golden brown and firm to touch. Remove from pan to cool.

sources.name: Sour Cream Coffee Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease a deep 9-inch Bundt mold with butter and dust with flour. Set aside.
In bowl, stir together the filling mixture until well mixed and set aside.
In stand mixer, cream butter and maple crystals. Add eggs one at a time, and beat until well incorporated. Add sour cream and mix until batter is smooth. Add vanilla.
Sift together flour, salt, and baking soda. Add dry ingredients to wet in stand mixer, and mix until batter is smooth.
Pour batter in prepared cake pan. Sprinkle crumble mixture over batter. Pour remainder of batter atop filling.
Bake cake for 35-40 minutes, or until a toothpick or skewer inserted in cake comes out smooth.
Let cake sit in pan for approximately 15 minutes before unmolding onto cooling rack. Cook cake completely before slicing.

sources.name: Vegan and Gluten-Free Chocolate Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (convection oven to 300°F). Oil and flour 9-inch square pan and line with parchment.
In bowl, whisk together almond flour, sorghum flour, tapioca flour, cocoa powder, salt, and baking powder. Process to combine. Transfer dry ingredients to bowl.

In separate bowl set over simmering water, melt 1 cup of chocolate and coconut oil. Remove from heat and whisk chocolate and coconut oil together. Stir in kuzu-water mixture, coconut sugar, coconut milk, and vanilla. Whisk wet ingredients to emulsify.
Pour wet mixture into dry and stir well. The batter should be stiff. Fold in walnuts and remaining 1/4 cup chocolate.
Transfer batter to pan, place parchment atop brownie. Smooth surface with hands until even.
Bake 30 minutes. Cool in pan for about 1 hour (otherwise brownie will crack when cut). Cut edges of brownie away from sides of pan before removing from pan.

sources.name: SPICE LOAF RING

lines.name: softened butter
lines.notes: 3 sticks; + 1-2 teaspoons butter for greasing pan

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour 9 or 10-inch non-stick Bundt pan.
In food processor, combine butter and maple crystals. Process 2-3 minutes. Add eggs one at a time. Add almond extract. Continue to blend 2-3 minutes longer. Transfer to medium bowl.
In separate medium bowl, sift together flours, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and salt.
Fold flour mixture into butter egg mixture (batter will be slightly thick).
Pour batter into Bundt pan (should be about 2/3 full).
Bake for 25-30 minutes. Cool in pan about 10 minutes. Run knife around edge to loosen cake from pan. Cool completely on rack.

sources.name: TOASTED WALNUT CRUST (FOR LIGHT LEMON TART)
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil and parchment 8 or 9-inch tart pan. Alternatively, use 5-6 four-inch, non-stick paper tart pans.
Combine nuts, flour, maple crystals, and salt in food processor. Grind to fine meal.
Add syrup and oil to processor. Pulse to form dough.
Place dough in middle of tart pan. Using your fingertips, press dough out so that bottom and sides are evenly covered. Trim crust and discard any excess. Blot excess oil from crust with paper towel.
Transfer tart pan(s) to refrigerator for 10-15 minutes to chill.
Transfer tart pan(s) to sheet tray and bake about 20 minutes. Cool completely before filling.

sources.name: FRESH BERRY TART WITH NUT CRUST
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil 9-inch tart pan or use 5-6 four-inch, non-stick paper tart pans.
In food processor, grind pecans to fine meal with flour, maple crystals, baking powder, and salt.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil and maple syrup.
Add oil and syrup to dry ingredients in processor. Pulse lightly until dough comes together.
Press crust mixture into tart pan(s). Refrigerate 15-20 minutes, then bake 20-25 minutes. Let cool completely.
In small pot, simmer agar flakes in apple juice until agar completely dissolves. Add kuzu/juice slurry. Whisk until mixture thickens. Add maple syrup, pinch of salt, and berries.
Cook 6-8 minutes. Remove from heat and let mixture cool partially. Pour filling into cooled crust.
Let set completely. Garnish with mint before serving. There may be filling left over. Puree in food processor to make pudding.

sources.name: CURRANT SCONES
steps: Pre-heat oven to 350° F.
Sift and whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, and maple crystals.
Cut butter into dry mix to form coarse crumbs.
In another bowl, beat egg, heavy cream, zest and currants together.
Add wet to dry until just combined.
Fold out onto table and form semi-flattened log.
Cut log into triangles and bake on parchment for 10 minutes.
Serve warm.
Note: If using rice flour add more liquid (about 2 tablespoons).

sources.name: CAROB CAKE WITH WALNUTS

lines.name: walnuts
lines.notes: coarsely chopped (optional for top of cake)

steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil and flour one 8-inch cake pan and line bottom with parchment.
Combine dry ingredients in bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared baking pan.
Sprinkle walnuts on top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.

sources.name: GENOISE
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with lightly buttered or oiled parchment.

Add eggs, coconut sugar, and vanilla to stand mixer bowl and beat at high speed for about 6-10 minutes until mixture has tripled in volume and has become light in color and foamy. Mixture should be almost consistency of stiff peaks.
Gently transfer egg mixture into clean large bowl. Sift flour in small batches (3 times) into egg mixture while folding batter with large rubber spatula.
Divide batter into 2 prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes or until cake is golden brown and springy to touch.
Using paring knife, cut cake away from sides of pan immediately, leaving cake in pans to cool for 10 minutes.
Remove cakes from pans, remove parchment from bottoms of cakes, and cool completely on wire racks. Use cakes as two layers or split each of them and use as four layers.

sources.name: SHORTBREAD COOKIES
steps: Preheat oven to 300° F and line half sheet tray with parchment paper.
Cream butter, sugar, vanilla and salt in stand mixer.
Gradually sift in flour until well mixed.

Firmly press dough into flattened 6-inch oval in center of sheet tray. Cut dough into 16 equal-sized slices and pierce each slice with fork in decorative design (be sure to pierce through to pan to allow excess steam to escape).
Bake about 45-50 minutes or until entire dough is golden brown and firm to touch.
Remove from oven and cool on wire rack. Retrace cuts in dough to loosen cookies but allow to remain on sheet tray to fully cool (do not move cookies as they are very fragile at this stage).

sources.name: BLACK AND WHITE COOKIES
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection). Line 2 half-sheet pans with parchment paper.
Whisk together flours, baking powder, salt and lemon zest in bowl and set aside.
Beat eggs and sugar in bowl until smoothly blended. Add milk, butter, and vanilla extract.
Slowly add egg/sugar mixture into flour mixture, blending until smooth.
Using 1-ounce scoop, drop cookies 2 inches apart on sheet tray. Bake for about 15 minutes, until lightly golden and tops feel firm to touch.
Remove cookies to wire racks and cool at room temperature before frosting.
Whisk confectioner's sugar in bowl with 2-3 tablespoons boiling water until thick but smooth.

Remove frosting from heat and reserve 3 tablespoons of frosting to make 'black' frosting; use remainder to frost half of each cookie (if frosting becomes too thick, add drops of boiling water again until it is spreadable).
Melt chocolate in small bowl over simmering water. Stir in corn syrup.

Add reserved white frosting to chocolate and stir to spreadable consistency (adding more hot water, if necessary, to thin). Spread bare half of each cookie with chocolate frosting. Set cookies aside until frostings set.

sources.name: GHIRARDELLI AWARD WINNING CHOCOLATE BROWNIES
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F (325° F in convection oven). Grease and flour 8 x 8-inch square baking pan and line with parchment paper.
Whisk eggs with sugar and vanilla; add melted butter.
Whisk together dry ingredients (cocoa, flour, baking powder, and salt) and fold into egg mixture. Add nuts.
Bake for 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in middle of brownie comes out clean.

sources.name: Peanut Butter Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare 2 sheet trays with parchment paper.
Cream sugars and butter in stand mixer until light and fluffy.
Add egg, peanut butter, and vanilla to butter-sugar mixture.
Whisk together flour, salt, and soda and add to mixer until dough is smooth.
Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, place dough balls every 2 inches on half-sheet trays.
Press cookies flat with fork. Bake 15 minutes.

sources.name: Big Chewy Oatmeal-Raisin Cookies
steps: Heat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare 2 half sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, beat butter with sugars until creamy, approximately 3 minutes. Beat in egg.
Separately whisk flour, salt, baking powder, and nutmeg together. Add dry ingredients into butter-sugar mixture. Stir in oats and optional raisins.
Form dough into 24 (1-inch) balls using 1-ounce scoop, placing each cookie every 2 inches apart on sheet trays.
Bake until cookie edges turn golden brown, 20 to 25 minutes. Halfway during baking, rotate trays front to back and switch them from top to bottom.
Slide cookies cooling rack and let cool at least 15 minutes before serving.

sources.name: Carrot Cake

lines.name: crushed pineapple
lines.notes: 4 oz.; drained and squeezed to extract all liquid

steps: Preheat oven to 350° F (300° F in convection oven). Prepare miniature muffin tins with muffin papers.
Whisk dry ingredients together in large bowl.
Whisk together wet ingredients. Add raisins and walnuts.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and mix. Using 1-ounce ice cream scoop, fill muffin papers 2/3 full and bake for 25-30 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

sources.name: Fudgy Chocolate Cake
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil one 8-inch cake pan. Dust pan with 2 teaspoons of cocoa powder. Line bottom of pan with parchment paper.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Add finely chopped chocolate and mix to combine. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 35-40 minutes until cake is springy to touch and pulls away from sides.
Cool in pan on wire rack 10-15 minutes. Remove from pan and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: Vanilla Cake
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection oven). Oil and flour one 8-inch cake pan. Line bottom of pan with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 30-40 minutes until cake is springy to touch and pulls away from sides of pan.
Cool in pan on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pan and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: Zesty Lemon Cake
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pans.
Cool in pans on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: Orange Cake
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 15-20 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pan.
Cool in pans on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: Spiced Carrot Cake
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together dry ingredients in large bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
In separate bowl, whisk together wet ingredients and pour into dry. Mix well. Add additional ingredients and mix to combine.
Pour batter into prepared pans.
Bake for about 45-50 minutes until cakes are springy to touch and pull away from sides of pans.
Cool in pans on wire rack for about 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and allow to completely cool on rack.

sources.name: GINGER CAKE
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottoms with parchment.
Sift together flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves in medium bowl and whisk together to combine. Set aside.
Place softened butter in bowl of stand mixer. On low speed, mix just until butter is fluffy. Add sea salt and maple crystals; mix until creamy and well combined, about 2 minutes.

Add one egg at a time. Slowly add in maple syrup, orange juice, milk, and extracts. Combine on medium speed until well incorporated (mixture may look curdled, but will come back together once remaining ingredients are added).
Spoon combined dry ingredients into mixer a little at a time and mix until completely incorporated into butter mixture, scraping down sides of bowl as necessary.
Pour batter into 2 prepared pans. Bake about 20 minutes or until tops are golden brown and springy to touch.
Cool on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: BANANA CAKE
steps: Heat oven to 350°F (300°F in convection). Oil and flour two 8-inch cake pans and line bottom of pans with parchment.
In medium bowl, sift together dry ingredients. Whisk to combine.
In food processor, combine wet ingredient and process until smooth.
Using rubber spatula, transfer wet ingredients from food processor to bowl with dry ingredients. Mix to combine.
Pour batter into two prepared pans. Bake about 20-25 minutes or until top are golden brown, and cakes are springy to touch.
Cool on wire rack for 10-15 minutes. Remove from pans and completely cool on rack.

sources.name: KABOCHA SQUASH PIE
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Place squash cut side down on parchment-lined half sheet pan and bake until fork tender, approximately 1 hour.
Discard squash seeds and pulp (or save seeds for toasting). Scoop and reserve 2 cups of squash from its skin for this recipe.
Prepare an ice bath.

Puree squash, maple crystals, spices, and salt in food processor until smooth. Transfer mixture to 2 1/2 quart pot and slowly whisk in milk and cream. Simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens, about 3-5 minutes. Remove pot from heat and place in ice bath for 10 minutes before slowly whisking in eggs.
Pour filling into pie shell and bake for 30-40 minutes or until filling is lightly cracked around edges and center jiggles slightly. Cool for 1 hour before slicing.

sources.name: SWEET POTATO PECAN PIE
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Roll out pie dough and line pie plate. After dough has rested in refrigerator for 15 minutes, trim and form edges, cover and chill for another 30 minutes.
In bowl of food processor, combine yams, maple crystals, kuzu and soymilk, oil, spices, and extracts. Process until well blended, scraping sides of bowl often.

In 2 1/2 quart pot, over medium heat, bring agar and water to boil. Reduce heat, cover, and cook until agar is dissolved. Add agar mixture to yam mixture in food processor and blend for 1-2 minutes. Set aside.
Combine maple syrup and rice syrup and set aside.
Pour filling into pie shell. Arrange pecans on top of filling and drizzle syrup mixture over top of pie.
Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake for 40 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean and crust is firm. Remove foil from edges 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool pie to set filling before serving (about 30 minutes).

sources.name: CRANBERRY PEAR PIE
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Roll out first pie dough and line pie plate. After dough rests in refrigerator for 15 minutes, trim edges, cover, and chill for at least 30 minutes more. Roll out second dough and cut into 1/2 inch x 10 inch strips. Transfer strips to baking sheet, cover, and chill until ready to use.
In 2 1/2 quart sauce pan, combine cranberries, syrup, and orange juice. Bring to boil and reduce to simmer for 5 minutes or until all cranberries have popped. Add pears or apples.
Stir in arrowroot slurry and cook until mixture loses chalky appearance and thickens, about 1 minute. Transfer mixture to bowl to cool.
Spoon cooled filling into chilled pie shell. Arrange lattice strips on top. Trim ends of strips flush with overhang of shell and form edge.
Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Remove foil from edges 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool and set pie before serving (at least 30 minutes).

sources.name: SWEET CRANBERRY TART

lines.name: kuzu dissolved in 1/3 cup orange juice

steps: In 1-gallon pot, mix cranberries, maple syrup, and currants. Bring mixture to boil, reduce to simmer, and cook until all cranberries have popped.
In 2 1/2 quart pot, bring apple juice and agar to boil. Reduce heat and cook until agar is dissolved. Stir into cranberry mixture.
Mix together kuzu/orange juice slurry and orange zest. Stir kuzu slurry into cranberry mixture and cook until mixture is clear. Remove from heat and add walnuts. Chill to cool.
Spoon filling into baked tart shell and chill to set.

sources.name: SWISS BURNT PECAN TART

lines.name: barley malt syrup dissolved in 2 teaspoons water

steps: Preheat oven to 275°F.
Roast pecans for about 40 minutes. Remove from pan and allow to completely cool.
Raise oven temperature to 350°F.
Roll out half the dough and transfer to tart pan. Chill 15 minutes. Trim edges, allowing 1-inch overhang. Chill rolled dough for another 15 minutes.
Roll out other half of dough and transfer to sheet pan. Cover and chill until ready to use.
In bowl of food processor, grind pecans to coarse flour. Add syrups, arrowroot, and vanilla. Mix to combine.
Pour filling into tart shell. Place top dough over filling, trim and seal edges. Cut a few steam vents.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until crust is firm. Brush top with glaze 10 minutes before removing from oven.
Cool and set before serving (about 30 minutes).

sources.name: CORNMEAL CRUST
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Combine cornmeal, pecans, and oats in food processor. Grind to fine meal.

Whisk together oil, maple syrup, and sea salt. Add wet ingredients to dry in processor until cookie-like dough is formed. Press dough into lightly oiled tart pan. Bake tart 12-15 minutes or until firm and lightly browned. Cool.

sources.name: APPLE CRUMB PIE
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Roll out pie dough and line pie plate. Trim and form edges, cover, and chill for at least 30 minutes.

In small bowl, whisk together flours. In separate bowl, whisk together oil and maple syrup. Slowly drizzle oil and maple syrup mixture into flour mixture. Stir lightly to form small, moist crumbs. Cover and chill.
In 10-inch sauté pan, heat oil. Add apple slices and sauté until apples are slightly softened. Set aside to partially cool.
In large bowl, combine apples, maple syrup, lemon juice, vanilla, spices, salt, and flour. Toss until apples are well coated.
Place filling in pie shell. Top with crumbs. Loosely cover crust with tented foil to keep edges from browning too quickly.
Bake pie for 40-45 minutes or until apples are tender and crust is firm. Remove foil 10 minutes before removing pie from oven.
Cool pie before serving.

sources.name: FRENCH WALNUT TART

lines.name: arrowroot dissolved in 2 tablespoons cold water

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F.

Roll out first dough and transfer to tart pan; chill for 15 minutes. Trim edges of rolled dough, allowing 1-inch overhang. Cover and chill for 30 minutes more. Roll out other half of dough and transfer to sheet pan. Cover and chill until ready to use.
In one-gallon pot, combine sweeteners. Bring to boil, lower heat and add lemon juice, salt, almond milk, and walnuts.
Whisk in nut butter, extracts, and brandy. Add arrowroot slurry. Mix on medium low heat until mixture thickens slightly. Remove from heat and cool.
Pour walnut mixture into tart shell. Place top dough over filling, trim and seal edges. Cut a few steam vents.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until crust is firm and golden.
Cool before serving (about 25 minutes).
Note: If cashew butter is very thick, loosen it up with 1-2 tablespoons of water or nut milk.

sources.name: CARAMELIZED ONION TART
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter or oil 9-inch tart pan with removable bottom.
Roll crust between parchment; chill for 15 minutes. Transfer crust to prepared pan and rest in fridge again for 30 minutes more.
Heat butter or oil in 12-inch sauté pan over medium/low heat. Add onions and cook over (stirring occasionally) until caramelized, about 20 minutes.
While onions cook, half blind bake tart crust (with pie weights) for approximately 10-12 minutes (or until lightly golden).
Remove crust from oven; turn temperature down to 335°F.
Spread caramelized onions into tart shell (do not pat down).
Whisk together custard ingredients and pour over onions.
Bake until custard is set and crust is golden brown, approximately 12-15 minutes.

sources.name: COCONUT-LIME CREAM TART
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F. Oil 9-inch tart pan with removable bottom.

Using your fingertips, blend together flour, macadamias, shredded coconut, maple crystals, salt and coconut oil until mixture resembles coarse meal. Press mixture into tart pan. Refrigerate for 15-20 minutes. Bake for 10-15 minutes or until golden brown. Set aside to cool.

Combine coconut milk into 2 1/2 quart saucepan with agar flakes, rum, maple syrup, brown rice syrup and salt. Bring to boil over medium heat, lower heat and simmer (whisking occasionally) about 30 minutes or until agar is completely dissolved.

In second 2 1/2 quart saucepan, combine semolina flour and cold water. Over high flame, whisk constantly until mixture thickens (consistency should resemble thick cream of wheat). Turn off heat and whisk into coconut milk mixture. Add lime juice and zest. Whisk to combine.
Pour filling into large bowl to cool, stirring constantly, to prevent mixture from setting up. When filling is warm (not hot), pour into cooled tart shell. Garnish with toasted coconut and lime zest.

sources.name: SHEPHERD’S PIE

lines.name: arrowroot dissolved in 3 teaspoons cold water

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Partially 'blind bake' pie shell (about 10 minutes) and set aside.
In 10-inch sauté pan, heat olive oil. Add onion, garlic, carrots, parsnips, and fresh thyme. Sauté until slightly tender. Add couple tablespoons water to deglaze pan.
Mix together sesame oil, tamari, and mustard; stir into vegetable mixture in sauté pan. Continue to cook another 10 minutes, and transfer mixture to bowl.
In separate 10-inch sauté pan, heat olive oil, add seitan and cook until seitan is slightly browned. Add wine and continue cooking until wine is absorbed. Add seitan to bowl with cooked vegetables.

Thicken reduced stock by adding arrowroot slurry and simmering until mixture thickens. Add this mixture to bowl containing vegetables and seitan. Season mixture with salt and pepper to taste. Set aside to cool.
In 1-gallon pot, boil potatoes until tender. Drain. Process potatoes through ricer or food mill. Season with soy milk, butter or olive oil, salt and pepper. Cover and set aside.
Fill partially baked pie shell with vegetable/seitan mixture. Using pastry bag fitted with tip, pipe potato mixture onto top of pie.
Bake for about 20-25 minutes or until vegetables are fork tender and crust is fully baked. Remove from oven and garnish with chopped parsley.

sources.name: GLUTEN-FREE SWEET POTATO PECAN TART

lines.name: gluten free breadcrumbs mixed with 2 tablespoons maple crystals
whole pecans or 1 cup thick coconut flakes

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and lightly grease tart pan with small amount of softened butter or oil.

Grind pecans and maple crystals to fine meal in food processor. Add flours and pulse to combine about 30 seconds more. Transfer mixture from food processor to bowl. In separate bowl, whisk together melted butter, water and, salt. Pour wet mixture into dry and mix to combine. If mixture is too moist, refrigerate for 5-10 minutes before pressing out crust.
Press crust mixture into tart pan. Refrigerate 15-20 minutes or until crust is firm to touch. Pierce crust with fork and partially bake for 15-20 minutes. Cool before filling.
Before filling tart shell, sprinkle breadcrumbs and maple crystals over crust (this prevents crust from getting soggy).
In food processor, puree yams. Add syrup, eggs, cream, vanilla, ginger juice, ground spices, and salt. Blend until mixture is creamy and smooth. Transfer puree to partially baked pie shell.
Decorate top of tart with pecans and brush nuts with maple syrup or top with coconut (omitting maple syrup wash).
Bake tart 30-35 minutes until filling is just firm. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

sources.name: OLIVE OIL CRUST
steps: In medium bowl, sift together flour, salt and baking powder.

Cut oil into flour mixture all at once but do not mix. Toss flour around lightly coating fat to create little balls of flour coated fat. A light touch is important here. Final blending will take place on pastry board in rolling.
Add just enough water (one tablespoon at a time) to form ball, being careful not over-mix and create too much gluten.
Flatten dough into disc, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate for 15 minutes to relax the dough. Roll to desired shape. Transfer rolled dough to pie or tart pan and chill for 30 minutes or more.
Heat oven to 375°F, fill crust and bake.

sources.name: SESAME PRESSED CRUST

lines.name: chilled juice or water to bind

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Oil 9-inch pie or tart pan.
Process together whole wheat pastry flour, oatmeal, sesame seeds and salt until mixture is uniformly flour-like.
Whisk together oil and syrup.
Add oil-syrup mixture to processor and mix until thoroughly combined. Add juice or water if more liquid is needed.
With wet fingertips, press mixture into oiled pie plate.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden.

sources.name: ROLLED FIG COOKIES

lines.name: blanched almonds
lines.notes: 1/4 cup + 2 tablespoons; ground to fine meal (measure then grind)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line two half-sheet trays with parchment paper and set aside.
In food processor, sift together flours, almond meal, and cinnamon. In small bowl, whisk together salt, syrup, and oil.
Add wet mixture to dry in food processor. Pulse to combine.
Divide dough evenly in half. Flatten dough into 2 discs and wrap each in plastic wrap. Refrigerate 10-15 minutes to firm.
In 2-quart pot, combine figs, apple juice, vanilla, cinnamon, cloves, and salt. Simmer 5-7 minutes or until figs are softened. Drain figs, reserving cooking liquid.
Puree fig mixture in food processor, adding cooking liquid as necessary, to make smooth, spreadable paste. Set aside to cool.
Roll each dough separately on parchment paper (dough should be about 1/8 inch thick. Trim excess dough so that dough roughly measures 10” by 6” rectangle.

Spread cooled or room temperature filling over rolled out dough. Roll dough jelly roll style as tightly as possible. Wrap dough in parchment paper and transfer to freezer for 15-20 minutes until hard.
Using bread knife, slice dough into ¼-inch rounds. Transfer to sheet trays and bake 10-15 minutes or until lightly golden. Cool and serve.

sources.name: JAM DOT COOKIES

lines.name: extra virgin canola oil
lines.notes: olive oil, melted butter OR 6 tablespoons melted coconut oil

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Grind almonds, flour, oats, and cinnamon in food processor to fine meal.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil, maple syrup, and sea salt. Add liquid to dry mixture in food processor and mix until well combined.

Form cookies using level 1-ounce scoop. Round them into walnut sized balls. Place on baking sheet and form indentation in middle of cookie using floured ¼ teaspoon measure. Fill indentation with about ½ teaspoon of jam and bake 15-20 minutes or until golden.

sources.name: WALNUT TEA COOKIES
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
Cream butter and maple crystals in stand mixer until fluffy and well combined, about 5 minutes. Add vanilla and salt until mixed.

In separate smaller bowl, whisk together flours. Slowly sift flours into butter mixture in stand mixer, until all flour is incorporated. Add in walnuts. Divide dough in 2 and wrap each in plastic. Refrigerate 10-15 minutes.
Remove 1 dough from refrigerator. Roll between parchment paper to 1/4" thickness. Freeze dough until hard. Cut shapes from dough using cookie cutters. Repeat process with second dough.
Bake about 6 minutes. Rotate baking pans and continue to bake about 5-6 more minutes or until lightly golden. Remove cookies from pans to racks to cool.

sources.name: CHOCOLATE CHERRY PECAN BARS
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Oil, flour, and parchment line 9-inch by 9-inch square baking pan.

In stand mixer, beat butter, date sugar, maple crystals, and vanilla until fluffy. In bowl, whisk together all-purpose and whole wheat pastry flours. Slowly sift flours into butter mixture until combined.
Press dough in even layer in prepared pan. Bake for about 10 minutes (rotate pan half way through cooking to ensure even baking) or until edges are lightly browned. Set aside to cool.
In stand mixer, beat date sugar, maple crystals, flour, salt, vanilla, and eggs until smooth. Stir in pecans, cherries, orange zest, and chocolate chips and mix just to combine.
Spread filling over crust to create even layer. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until edges are golden brown and filling is set.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes before unmolding onto cooling rack. Transfer to freezer to cool completely before cutting into bars.

sources.name: Raspberry Shortbread Linzer Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line two half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, cream butter and maple crystals together until fluffy.

Whisk together flours and arrowroot in separate medium bowl. Slowly sift flour mixture into butter mixture while continuing to mix until well combined. Add cashews and continue to mix until incorporated. Divide dough equally into 2 and wrap each piece in plastic. Chill in refrigerator for 15-20 minutes, until dough firms.

Roll out both doughs to about 1/8” thickness. Freeze dough until hard. Cut dough with lightly floured cookie cutters. For each cookie, cut solid bottom and mate with center cut out using smaller cutter. Continue process until all dough is used.

Place cookies on 2 sheet trays (bottoms on one tray and tops with centers cut out on other). Bake about 5-6 minutes and rotate pans. Continue to bake until edges are lightly browned. Remove from pans and cool on racks.

When cool, spread 1 tablespoon preserves on solid cookie bottom. Lightly sprinkle cookie tops (with holes) with powdered sugar, if using. Carefully press top cookie with hole on jam-topped bottom. Continue process until all cookies are assembled.

sources.name: Chocolate Biscotti
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line one half-sheet tray with parchment paper.
In small double boiler, melt chocolate chips. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature.
In bowl whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
Using stand mixer, mix butter, maple crystals, and melted chocolate. Add egg whites. Blend one minute more. Scrape sides of bowl with spatula and blend another thirty seconds.
Add dry ingredients (flour, cocoa, baking soda, salt) to mixer to combine. Dough will very sticky. Divide dough in two.
Roll each dough in chopped nuts and then form each into log shape on sheet tray (6 inches apart). Flatten logs into length of about 8 1/2 inches and width of 3 inches.
Bake 20 minutes or until firm to touch. Remove from oven, lower heat to 300° F, let logs cool 10-12 minutes.
Using bread knife, slice logs into 1/4 inch to 1/2 inch diagonal slices.
Cook slices 7-10 minutes more on each side. Cool and serve. (These get crunchier as they sit.)

sources.name: Pecan Tuiles

lines.name: pecans
lines.notes: toasted in oven and coarsely chopped

lines.name: melted coconut oil or canola oil

steps: Preheat convection oven to 300° F (350° F in conventional oven). Line 5 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
Transfer chopped pecans to medium bowl and add flour and arrowroot. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl, whisk oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt until thoroughly combined. Add to pecan/flour mixture, mixing until combined. Let batter sit for 15 minutes.

Use teaspoon measure to drop batter onto Silpat-lined baking sheets. Place only 5 cookies per sheet – one in each corner and one in middle. Bake one sheet at a time for 10 minutes until cookies are bubbly.

Cool cookies for approximately 30 seconds before removing from Silpats. Working quickly (because cookies cool and set hard very fast), remove tuiles from sheet tray using small offset spatula and wrap around cannoli molds. Repeat procedure with remaining sheet trays until all batter is used.

sources.name: Gluten-Free Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 375° F. Line 2 half-sheet pans with parchment paper.
In medium bowl whisk sorghum flour, buckwheat flour, tapioca starch flour, brown rice flour, white sweet rice flour, and baking powder together. Set aside.
Cream butter and maple crystals with paddle attachment in stand mixer.
Add egg, vanilla, and salt to butter/maple crystal mixture, and salt. Beat on slow speed for 30-60 seconds more.
Stop mixer and add flour mixture to other ingredients. Mix to combine. (Mixture will be stickier than type of “drop” batter prepared with wheat flour.) Add chocolate chips.
Using 1-ounce scoop, portion dough onto baking sheets. Place approximately dozen cookies per sheet with good distance between, as cookies spread.
Cook for about 7-10 minutes or until cookies are nicely golden (do not under-bake).
Transfer to racks until cooled and firmed up.

sources.name: GLUTEN-FREE CRISP GINGER COOKIE
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F. Line 3 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
In medium bowl whisk almond meal, sorghum flour, arrowroot flour, ground ginger, and black pepper.
In separate small bowl, whisk together oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, water, and salt.
Pour syrup mixture into nut/flour mixture. Batter should be consistency of heavy cream. If it is too thick, add more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you have proper consistency.

Using teaspoon measure, drop batter onto sheets (5-6 cookies a sheet). Decorate each cookie with one sliced almond. Bake 15-20 minutes or until cookies are golden. Cool before removing from sheet pan.
Note: Cookies hold shape better on Silpat.

sources.name: Phyllo Triangles with Feta and Kale

lines.name: ricotta cheese
lines.notes: strained 30 minutes in strainer lined with wet cheesecloth

steps: Heat convection oven to 350°F. Line half sheet tray with parchment. Set aside.
In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil over medium flame. Sweat onion, garlic, ½ teaspoon salt, nutmeg, and red pepper flakes until onions are translucent. Set aside.

In 2-gallon pot, bring 1 gallon water to boil with remaining 1 tablespoon salt. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch kale until tender, about 3-5 minutes. Shock in ice water and drain in colander. Squeeze excess moisture from kale and finely chop.
Return pan with onions to burner over medium flame and add kale. Sauté mixture until kale is heated through.
When mixture has cooled, transfer to medium bowl. Add feta and ricotta cheeses and mix to combine. Season to taste.
Unwrap phyllo and lay one sheet on parchment paper horizontally. Cover remaining sheets with damp towel. Brush phyllo with butter.

Spoon seven 1-tablespoon dollops of mixture across bottom edge of phyllo at equal distances. Cut phyllo into strips between each dollop, and fold up “flag” style (see diagram) to make triangular shape. Transfer finished phyllo triangles to prepared sheet pan. Brush tops with more butter. Repeat with remaining phyllo.
Just before baking, brush all triangles with butter again. Bake 20 minutes or until evenly golden.

sources.name: Phyllo Triangles with Tofu and Spinach

lines.name: spinach
lines.notes: stemmed, steamed, and wrung of excess moisture

steps: Heat convection oven to 350°F. Line half sheet tray with parchment. Set aside.
Press tofu between paper towels on sheet pan with weighted plate for amount 30 minutes. Transfer tofu to medium bowl and crumble it with fingertips. Set aside.

In 12-inch sauté pan, heat oil over medium flame. Sweat shallots, salt, fennel, cumin, and paprika until shallots are translucent. Transfer mixture to bowl with tofu. Add miso and umeboshi. Mix to combine. Chop spinach and combine with tofu mixture. Season to taste.
Unwrap phyllo and lay one sheet on parchment paper horizontally. Cover remaining sheets with damp towel. Brush phyllo with oil.

Spoon seven 1-tablespoon dollops of mixture across bottom edge of phyllo at equal distances. Cut phyllo into strips between each dollop, and fold up “flag” style (see diagram) to make triangular shape. Transfer finished phyllo triangles to prepared sheet pan. Brush tops with more oil. Repeat with remaining phyllo.
Just before baking, brush all triangles with butter again. Bake 20 minutes or until evenly golden.

sources.name: RUGELACH
steps: In food processor, combine cream cheese and butter. Process until smooth and creamy. Add maple crystals and vanilla; process until incorporated, scraping sides of bowl as necessary.
In small bowl, whisk together flour and salt. Add to food processor. Pulse until dough starts to clump together and form ball.
Remove dough from food processor. Separate dough equally in two and wrap each piece in plastic and flatten to disc shape. Refrigerate for at least one and one half hours until firm.
In medium bowl, combine currants, walnuts, maple crystals, and cinnamon. Set aside. Place preserves into separate small bowl. Set aside.
Pre-heat oven to 350°F, line 2 half sheet pans with parchment paper.

Work with one dough at a time, leaving other in refrigerator. Liberally dust dough with flour. Roll between 2 pieces of plastic wrap to 9-inch circle. Thickness should be 1/8 inch. Use inverted nine-inch cake pan to trim edges.
Using offset spatula, spread dough with half of preserves. Sprinkle with 1/2 of filling. Divide circle into 16 even “slices” (using bench knife, pizza cutter, or sharp knife).
Starting at wide end of triangle, roll each slice tightly as possible. Transfer to sheet tray and refrigerate 15-20 minutes more. Repeat steps 7-10 with remaining dough.
Before baking, brush each cookie with egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes or until lightly golden.

sources.name: APPLE-OAT CRUMBLE

lines.name: granny smith apples
lines.notes: peeled, cored, cut in into 1/8-inch slices

steps: Pre-heat oven to 350°F. While cutting apples, soak slices in acidulated water (juice of 1/2 lemon and 4 cups water).
In large bowl, whisk together salt, arrowroot, cinnamon, maple crystals, and apple juice. Drain apples, and combine with cinnamon-maple mixture. Transfer to 9-inch square pan.
In medium bowl combine oats, flour, and cinnamon. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl whisk oil, syrup, and salt.
Pour wet into over dry and toss until mixture is completely coated.
Spread topping over apples. Bake 45 to 55 minutes until topping is golden and apples and filling is bubbly. Serve garnished with drizzle of pomegranate reduction.

sources.name: PHYLLO CUPS WITH SAUTÉED APPLES

lines.name: sticks melted butter or 1 cup no taste oil

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F degrees. Oil muffin tins (3 tins, 6 muffins each).
Layer 6 sheets of phyllo, brushing each layer with either melted butter or oil. Sprinkle each layer with pinch of maple crystals and pinch of cinnamon.
Cut layered phyllo into six equal pieces, making six 4-inch by 4-inch squares. Repeat process until all phyllo is used.
When all 18 squares are complete, carefully press them into muffin tins. Bake for 7-10 minutes or until phyllo cups are golden.
Remove cups from tins and cool. Fill with sautéed apples (recipe following) and ice cream. Garnish plate with cinnamon, toasted nuts, and fresh mint.
Heat clarified butter in 8-inch sauté pan until hot. Add apples and brown 3-5 minutes. With slotted spoon, transfer apples to warm plate.
Pour off clarified butter and deglaze with juice, then add syrup and vanilla or rum. Reduce by little more than half, or until bubbles cover surface of pan.
Cool sauce for minute or two. Mount with cold butter.
Transfer apples to phyllo cup. Coat apples with 1 to 2 tablespoons of sauce and dust with cinnamon and nuts. Top with ice cream. Use remaining sauce as underliner for phyllo cups.

sources.name: Golden Turmeric 'Panna Cotta' with Ginger-Pepper Lace Cookies
steps: Grease inside of small silicone molds with oil.

Combine agar flakes and milk in medium saucepan and simmer over medium heat until agar flakes have dissolved. Add cardamom, turmeric, ginger, maple syrup, vanilla bean, and salt. Simmer an additional 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Strain mixture through chinois and pour into silicone molds. Cool until firm.
In blender, puree blackberries and maple syrup. Strain coulis and transfer to squeeze bottle.
Preheat convection oven to 300°F. Line 5 half-sheet trays with Silpats.
Transfer pecans to medium bowl. Add flour and arrowroot. Whisk to combine.
In separate bowl, whisk oil, rice syrup, maple syrup, vanilla, ginger, black pepper, and salt. Add to pecan/flour mixture, mixing until combined. Let batter sit for 15 minutes.
Use teaspoon to drop batter onto Silpat-lined baking sheets. Place only 5 cookies per sheet – one in each corner and one in middle. Bake one sheet at a time for 10 minutes until cookies are bubbly.

Cool cookies for approximately 30 seconds before removing from Silpats. Working quickly (because cookies cool and set hard very fast), remove tuiles from sheet tray using small offset spatula and wrap around cannoli molds. Repeat procedure with remaining sheet trays until all batter is used.
Invert panna cotta onto plate. Garnish with tuile, blackberries, gold dust, blackberry coulis and mint sprigs.

sources.name: GLUTEN-FREE CHOCOLATE CAKE

lines.name: stick unsalted butter
lines.notes: melted + 1 tablespoon solid butter for greasing Bundt pan

steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease 9 1/2-inch Bundt pan with butter and dust with cocoa powder.
In food processor, blend dates with maple syrup.
When dates are thoroughly blended, add vanilla, eggs and melted butter. Mix to combine.
In medium bowl, sift together flours, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Whisk well to incorporate. Add to date-syrup mixture in food processor. Mix to combine.
Pour batter into baking pan, filling no more than 2/3 up side of cake pan. Any extra cake batter can be used for muffins. Do not overfill pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes. Allow cake to cool completely.
Double-melt chocolate and drizzle over cake. Sprinkle with walnuts.

sources.name: CHECKERBOARD COOKIES
steps: For vanilla dough: Preheat oven to 350° F. Line 2 half-sheet trays with parchment paper.
In stand mixer, beat together butter, maple crystals, and salt until light and fluffy with paddle attachment. Add egg and vanilla and continue to mix until well combined.

Whisk together flour and baking powder in separate small bowl. Add flour mixture to butter mixture in mixer until combined. Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate 10 minutes to firm up while making chocolate dough.
For chocolate dough: In stand mixer, beat together butter, maple crystals, and salt until well combined. Add egg, baking powder, and almond extract. Continue to mix until smooth.

Whisk together flour and cocoa powder in separate small bowl. Gradually sift flour/cocoa mixture into butter mixture and mix just until combined. Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate at least 10 minutes until firm.
For assembly: Divide vanilla dough into 5 equal pieces. Divide chocolate dough into 4 equal pieces.

On parchment, using flour as necessary for dusting, roll out each piece dough to 1/4 inch. Make 3 stacks of rolled dough, brushing each layer with egg white: 1) vanilla/chocolate/vanilla; 2) chocolate/vanilla/chocolate; 3) vanilla/chocolate/vanilla.

Using bench scraper, square off sides of each stack of dough. Freeze 3 stacks of dough until hard. Using sharp knife, cut lengthwise rectangles of each dough, brush them with egg white, and stack rectangles in same order as listed above. Cut crosswise at 1/4 inch intervals across rectangle stacks to form cookies. Trimmed scraps of dough can be bundled together and re-rolled, frozen and stamped with cookie cutter shapes to make marbleized cookies.
Transfer to sheet trays. Brush tops with egg white. Bake 6-10 minutes or until golden at edges. Remove from pans to racks to cool.

sources.name: VEGAN BAKLAVA
steps: Preheat oven to 300°F.
For phyllo: In bowl, mix nuts and cinnamon. Set aside.
In half-sheet pan lined with parchment paper, individually oil and layer 6-7 sheets of phyllo. Edges of phyllo sheets will overhang bottom of sheet pan slightly, but they will be trimmed later.

Spread portion of nut mixture (approximately 1/3-1/2 cups) over top of phyllo, enough to cover surface. Add another sheet of brushed phyllo and cover with more nuts; repeat this process until all nuts are gone.
Top baklava with 6 more layers of oil-brushed phyllo. Trim excess phyllo from sides of pan, so phyllo fits pan exactly.
Cut baklava into eighths lengthwise. Then make diagonal crosswise cuts, at 2-inch intervals.
Bake baklava 30 minutes at 300°F in standard oven (fan in convection oven causes phyllo to blow away). Bake additional 30 minutes at 350°F, until golden brown.
For syrup: While baklava bakes, bring all syrup ingredients to simmer in 2-quart saucepan. Cook syrup uncovered until reduced to 2 cups.
Remove baklava from oven. Pour hot syrup over warm phyllo and let sit at least 30 minutes.
